title: Learned CT block scores track reported opacity burden in a small COVID-19 cohort
summary: In 30 COVID-19 patients from an Italian CT cohort, a learned block-analysis score correlated with source-reported ground-glass-opacity values. The paper describes generating each patient’s score using a model trained without that patient. This is a small retrospective imaging association, not evidence that the score predicts clinical deterioration or measures physiological disease severity.
ai_technology: Random forest and related learned CT block classifiers
organization: Bennett University; University of Eastern Piedmont; AtheroPoint; University of Cagliari

evidence.tested: The source cohort contained 30 COVID-19 patients and 30 controls, contributing 705 and 990 CT slices respectively. Segmented lungs were divided into twelve spatial blocks and learned classifiers contributed to block-level scoring. For the specific patient-level association, Methods/Results state that all slices of each patient were scored by a system trained on all other patients. Appendix Table 12 lists 30 COVID-19 patients with the derived score and GGO values; the source reports correlation approximately 0.9145.
evidence.unknown: The score and GGO comparator describe the same images, rather than independent clinical outcomes or a causal mechanism. Small single-center retrospective data, sex imbalance and incomplete score-reference documentation limit interpretation. Image-level classification leaderboard metrics are omitted because their cross-validation description does not establish patient-disjoint partitions. The severity label used by the authors is not treated as a validated measure of prognosis, physiology or treatment need.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers distinguish CT-block feature distributions and contribute to a patient-level block score, enabling the represented comparison with reported CT-opacity values.

source_review.scope: Read actual cohort/reference and preprocessing Methods, learned classification/block-score workflow, explicit leave-patient-out score evaluation paragraph68 and full original Appendix Table12. Kept this patient-level opacity association separate from image-fold classification benchmarks. Original publisher January26 date read.
